info.name: Event Scoring App - Backend Regression Suite (T18)
info.description:
Postman Collection v2.1 regression suite covering every backend RPC/table built for the event-scoring app from QA0 through T17 (see event-scoring-app-plan.md). This is the living regression suite referenced by ticket T18 in the plan, replacing the originally-planned Insomnia collection now that tooling has switched to Yaak (Yaak imports this natively via Import > Postman; see README.md in this folder for import + run instructions).

Run order: folders are ordered to match the plan's Track A ticket sequence and are designed to run top-to-bottom in one pass (Auth first, T17 last). A few folders necessarily reorder some setup relative to strict ticket-build order so the suite is actually runnable end-to-end against the FINAL migrated schema (e.g. all fixture authoring — event/rounds/segments/questions — happens in the T6 folder, before activate_event freezes it; the T8a/QA4 folders that follow prove those freeze guardrails instead of repeating CRUD). Each folder's own description explains any such reordering. Several requests are timing-sensitive (server-authoritative answer windows + a 10s grace period) — see QA5/QA6/QA7's request descriptions.

item.name: QA0 - Event Format Enum + Immutability
item.description: QA0 ships public.event_format ('quiz' | 'judged') and prevent_event_format_change(), a BEFORE UPDATE trigger bound to events (in the now-skipped QA1 schema migration) that rejects any change to events.format once set. This is a pure schema/constraint ticket with no RPC or standalone endpoint to call — it is exercised implicitly every time the "Create Event" request (T6 folder) sets format='quiz' at insert, and would reject a PATCH that tried to change it afterward. No runtime request is included here by design.

item.name: QA2 - RLS (Negative Tests)
item.description: QA1 (skipped, schema-only) enables RLS with no policies on every table; QA2 (this ticket, also skipped as a folder for its own DDL) is the migration that actually writes the participant/grader/admin access model described in event-scoring-app-plan.md. These three requests are deliberately-403 negative tests, one per role, proving RLS denies writes outside each role's slice — order-independent (a nil UUID is used so these can run immediately after Auth, before any fixture data exists).

request.description: QA2 RLS: rounds_insert_organizer only allows the event organizer to insert. A participant attempting to insert a round (even against a non-existent event id — private.is_event_organizer() simply evaluates false and RLS rejects the row before any FK is checked) must be rejected. Proves the participant role cannot write event structure.

exec: pm.test("participant insert is rejected by RLS (403)", function () {

request.description: QA2 RLS: participants_insert_organizer only allows the event organizer to insert a participant row. A grader attempting the same insert (against a nil event id) must be rejected. Proves the grader role cannot write the roster.

exec: pm.test("grader insert is rejected by RLS (403)", function () {

request.description: QA2 RLS: answers_insert_own_open requires private.owns_participant(participant_id) — true only for the approved participant who owns that row. The organizer owns no participant row, so this insert (against nil participant/question/round/segment ids) must be rejected even though the organizer has broad structural access elsewhere. Proves "admin is read-only on answers".

exec: pm.test("organizer insert is rejected by RLS (403)", function () {

item.name: T6 - Event Lifecycle (activate_event)
item.description: Ships activate_event (draft -> active). Because activate_event requires round 1 (and, transitively, everything QA4/T8a's freeze triggers protect) to already exist, and because those freeze triggers make it impossible to author rounds/segments/questions AFTER activation, this folder also carries the full draft-phase fixture setup for the whole regression run: the event, both rounds, both segments, and all four questions (+ acceptable answers) used by every later folder. The T8a and QA4 folders that follow deliberately do NOT duplicate this creation step — they instead prove the freeze constraints those tickets actually added, which can only be demonstrated post-activation.

request.description: Prerequisite for activate_event: creates a draft quiz event owned by the admin/organizer, with grader_id set to the seeded grader test user (QA2's single-grader identity column — required for QA10's adjudicate_round_answers to authorize later). join_code is left out of the body so T10's events_generate_join_code trigger fills it; format='quiz' is set once and is immutable thereafter (QA0). Captures {{event_id}} and {{join_code}}.

item.name: [T8a] Negative: Round advancement_n Must Be Positive

request.description: Exercises T8a's rounds_advancement_n_positive CHECK constraint. Placed here (in the T6 folder) rather than in the T8a folder because it must run while the event is still draft — T8a's own folder runs after activate_event, by which point ANY new-round insert is already rejected by the separate "rounds cannot be added once left draft" trigger, which would mask this specific constraint. Expects a 400 check_violation.
Round 1 of 2. advancement_type=top_n, advancement_n=1 (only rank<=1 advances — matches the single seeded participant advancing cleanly with no tie). Captures {{round1_id}}.
Round 2 of 2, is_final_round=true (advancement_n must be null — rounds_final_has_no_advancement_n). Captures {{round2_id}}.

T6's activate_event(p_event_id): organizer-only, moves the event draft -> active. Quiz-format: requires round 1 to exist and be pending (verified above), opens round 1 (scoring_open, scoring_opened_at). Leaves the participant roster open (it freezes at the first reveal, QA5). Everything below this point runs against an ACTIVE event, so T8a's and QA4's freeze triggers are now live — that is deliberate: their own folders (next) exercise those freezes as negative tests instead of duplicating the CRUD already done above.

item.name: T8a - Round/Segment CRUD Guardrails
item.description: T8a's actual contribution is not new CRUD capability (organizer INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on rounds/segments already flows through QA2's RLS grants) but the constraints/triggers layered on top of it: advancement_n positivity, at-most-one-final-round, and the config freeze once an event leaves draft. The positivity and one-final-round constraints are exercised in the T6 folder (pre-activation, where a real CRUD attempt is still meaningful); this folder proves the freeze itself, which only means something post-activation. All three requests below are expected to fail (400) — that is the passing outcome.

item.name: QA3 - Participant Self-Register + Approve + Identity
item.description: Runs after activate_event (T6) but before the first reveal (QA5), so the QA5 roster-freeze trigger is not yet in effect and this folder is unaffected by the T6/T8a/QA4 reordering discussed above.

request.description: T10/QA3's join_event(p_join_code, p_name, p_type): self-registers the participant JWT holder as a pending participant of the event matching {{join_code}}. Idempotent on repeat calls. Captures {{participant_id}} (the participants.id row — distinct from {{participant_user_id}}, the auth.users id).
QA3's approve_participant(p_participant_id): organizer-only, moves the pending (or revoked) participant to admission_status=approved. Must run before the roster freezes at the first reveal (QA5).
QA3's my_participant_identity(p_join_code): resolves "who am I in this event" from just the join code. Should return the same row as Join Event, now with admission_status=approved.

item.name: QA4 - Question Authoring CRUD Guardrails
item.description: Like T8a, QA4 does not add a new RPC — it adds constraints/triggers on top of QA2's existing organizer CRUD grant. The positive-value check (window_seconds > 0) is exercised in the T6 folder (pre-activation); this folder proves the authoring-surface freeze once the event is active. All three requests are expected to fail (400) — that is the passing outcome. The actual question/acceptable-answer fixtures used by the rest of the suite were created in T6, before activation made this freeze relevant.

item.name: QA5 - Reveal + Server-Authoritative Window Close
item.description: Ships reveal_question (issues reveal_token, opens the window) and close_question_window (server-clock-gated close). Also ships the participant-roster freeze at first reveal (private.event_has_had_first_reveal) — QA3's join_event/approve_participant must run before this folder, which the collection order already guarantees.

request.description: QA5's reveal_question(p_question_id): organizer-only, requires the question pending in an active event whose round is scoring_open. Stamps revealed_at + a fresh reveal_token and opens the answer window (status=window_open). Captures {{question1_reveal_token}}. window_seconds=20, so downstream requests in this folder and QA6/QA7 are timing-sensitive — see each request's description.

QA5's close_question_window(p_question_id) only succeeds once window_seconds has actually elapsed since revealed_at — the server verifies the clock, not the caller. Called immediately after Reveal (0s elapsed < 20s), so this must be rejected. Expects a 400 check_violation.

exec: pm.test("closing before window_seconds elapses is rejected (400)", function () {

request.description: Run this at least 20s after "Reveal Question 1" above (configure a runner delay, or simply wait before sending it manually) — it is the real, successful close: status -> window_closed, window_closed_at stamped. QA6's submit_answer still accepts a late-but-in-grace submission afterward (window_seconds + 10s grace), so run QA6 promptly after this succeeds.

item.name: QA6 - Answer Submission API
item.description: Ships submit_answer. See the request description for the timing note: this call is deliberately positioned after QA5's close, so it demonstrates the disconnection-tolerance / grace-window acceptance path described in the plan, not a live in-window submit.

request.description: QA6's submit_answer(p_question_id, p_submitted_text, p_client_elapsed_ms, p_reveal_token, p_is_saved_draft): the single write path for both a live submit and a reconnect/sendBeacon draft replay. Runs after QA5 has already closed Question 1's window, so this exercises the grace-period acceptance path (question.status=window_closed but still within window_seconds+10s grace of revealed_at) rather than a live in-window submit — send this promptly after "Close Question Window" succeeds. p_client_elapsed_ms is the participant's own token-anchored timer, independent of real server-clock elapsed time. Captures {{answer1_id}}.

item.name: QA7 - Auto Pre-Mark Matcher
item.description: Ships auto_mark_question_answers plus the underlying normalize/numeric-parse/match helpers. Writes a provisional auto_correct that QA10's grader later confirms or overrides into final_correct.

request.description: QA7's auto_mark_question_answers(p_question_id): organizer-only batch pre-mark. Requires the question window_closed AND the same 10s grace period QA6 honors to have elapsed since window_closed_at (so a still-landing reconnect replay is never marked out from under itself) — if this returns a check_violation about the grace period, wait a few seconds and retry. Normalizes "Paris" against Question 1's acceptable-answer list and writes the provisional result to answers.auto_correct.

item.name: QA8 - Void Question
item.description: Ships void_question. Uses the dedicated throwaway "Question To Void" fixture from T6 rather than Question 1, so voiding it does not disturb the main live-play scoring path (QA6/QA7/QA10/T16).

request.description: Reuses QA5's reveal_question so the throwaway "Question To Void" (created in T6) has a real reveal_token before it is voided. Captures {{question3_reveal_token}} (unused downstream, captured for completeness).

QA8's void_question(p_question_id): organizer-only, one-way. Requires round 1 still scoring_open (this must run before QA9's Close Round 1). Discards the question's answers outright (there are none here) and marks it voided (voided_at/voided_by audit trail).

item.name: QA9 - Round-Close Gate
item.description: Ships close_round (using the final QA12-amended definition, which excludes is_tiebreak reserve-pool questions from the all-closed check).

request.description: QA9's close_round(p_round_id): organizer-only, requires every non-reserve question across the round's segments to be window_closed or voided. Round 1 has Question 1 (window_closed via QA5/QA6/QA7), the throwaway Question To Void (voided via QA8), and the is_tiebreak reserve question (excluded from this check per QA12's amendment — it stays pending). Sets round1.status=scoring_closed.

item.name: QA10 - Batched Single-Grader Adjudication
item.description: Ships adjudicate_round_answers. Authorizes against events.grader_id, which the T6 folder's "Create Event" request sets to {{grader_user_id}} up front.

request.description: QA10's adjudicate_round_answers(p_round_id, p_grades): grader-only (events.grader_id), requires the round scoring_closed. p_grades is a JSON array of {answer_id, final_correct}; confirms Question 1's answer as correct, writing final_correct/graded_by/graded_at.

item.name: T16 - calculate_results (Quiz Branch)
item.description: Ships calculate_results' quiz branch (sum final_correct) plus private.result_scope_totals (using the QA12-amended definition, which excludes is_tiebreak questions from every scope's total).

request.description: T16's calculate_results(p_event_id, p_round_id, p_segment_id, p_reason): organizer-only, requires the target round scoring_closed/advanced with no ungraded answers. Scope: p_round_id set, p_segment_id null = per-round leaderboard. Sums final_correct per participant, RANK()s, writes a new result_calculations header + frozen result_calculation_entries + an exclusion snapshot, flipping any prior is_final for the scope. Captures {{round1_calculation_id}}.

item.name: T16a - advance_round + declare_winner
item.description: Ships advance_round and declare_winner (final QA12-amended definitions, which consult a resolved sudden-death tiebreak at the boundary rank before falling back to co-advance). Because declare_winner requires the FINAL round to already be fully played and calculated — the same pipeline QA5 through T16 already demonstrated for round 1 — the "[Final Round Setup]" requests in this folder replay that pipeline once more against round 2's question before advance_round's final-round counterpart, declare_winner, is called. Same timing notes apply as QA5/QA6/QA7 (window_seconds=20s, 10s grace).

request.description: T16a's advance_round(p_round_id): non-final rounds only, requires scoring_closed with a final round-scope calculation already run (T16, above). Writes round_participants outcomes for round 1 (rank<=advancement_n=1 -> advanced), seeds round 2's round_participants with the advancing set, opens round 2 (scoring_open), and marks round 1 advanced.

declare_winner (below) requires the final round to already be scoring_closed with a final calculation — i.e. fully played. This replays QA5's reveal_question against the final round's question (round 2 is scoring_open after Advance Round 1 above). Captures {{question2_reveal_token}}.
Replays QA6's submit_answer, sent immediately after reveal (live in-window submit this time, unlike QA6's own grace-period demo). Captures {{answer2_id}}.

item.name: [Final Round Setup] Close Question Window - Question 2

request.description: Run at least 20s after "Reveal Question 2" above. Replays QA5's close_question_window.
Run at least 10s after the previous request (QA6/QA7's shared grace period). Replays QA7's auto_mark_question_answers.
Replays QA10's adjudicate_round_answers against the final round.
Replays QA9's close_round against the final round.

item.name: [Final Round Setup] Calculate Results - Final Round

request.description: Replays T16's calculate_results against the final round. Captures {{round2_calculation_id}}.

T16a's declare_winner(p_event_id): the final-round equivalent of advance_round. Requires the final round scoring_closed with a final calculation and an untied rank 1 (with only one seeded participant, this is trivially untied). Writes round_participants outcomes and sets events.winner_participant_id. Does not conclude the event (T17).

item.name: QA12 - Sudden-Death Tiebreak Sub-Flow
item.description: Ships tiebreaks/tiebreak_entrants/tiebreak_questions plus start_tiebreak, draw_tiebreak_question, void_tiebreak_question, and resolve_tiebreak_question. IMPORTANT: this suite's default fixture seeds exactly one participant (see the Auth folder), so round 1 never produces an actual tie and "Start Tiebreak" is expected to fail here with "no tie to break" — the requests below are still correctly shaped and independently callable. To exercise a real tie end-to-end: before Question 1 is revealed (QA5) — the roster freezes at first reveal — register and approve a second participant via a second GoTrue signup + QA3's join_event/approve_participant, then have both participants submit the same answer to Question 1 so round 1's calculate_results (T16) ranks them tied at rank 1 (advancement_n=1). Re-run this folder against that fixture to see start_tiebreak through resolve_tiebreak_question actually progress.

request.description: QA12's start_tiebreak(p_round_id): organizer-only, infers scope/cutoff from is_final_round and requires a genuine tie straddling the cutoff rank in that round's final calculate_results output (>=2 entries at rank=cutoff). EXPECTED TO FAIL in this fixture's default run: the suite seeds exactly one participant (Auth folder), so round 1 never has a tie to break. See this folder's description for how to actually exercise a tie. Captures {{tiebreak_id}} only if it succeeds.

QA12's draw_tiebreak_question(p_tiebreak_id): draws the next unused is_tiebreak reserve question (authored in T6) and reveals it in one step. Returns null (200, empty body) once the pool is exhausted. Requires {{tiebreak_id}} from a successful Start Tiebreak above.

Reuses QA6's submit_answer against the drawn tiebreak question. QA12 restricts writes to the frozen tiebreak_entrants cohort — a non-entrant is rejected even via this RPC. Requires {{drawn_tiebreak_question_id}} / {{drawn_tiebreak_reveal_token}} from a successful Draw Tiebreak Question above.

QA12's void_tiebreak_question(p_tiebreak_id): QA8's escape valve adapted for a tiebreak's already-scoring_closed round. Voids the currently-drawn, not-yet-graded question and frees the tiebreak to draw its next one.

QA12's resolve_tiebreak_question(p_tiebreak_id): requires the currently-drawn question window_closed/voided and fully graded. Computes cumulative sudden-death scores and checks for a clean cut at slots_to_fill; flips entrant outcomes and the tiebreak to resolved on a clean cut, otherwise leaves it open for another draw.

item.name: T17 - Conclude Event (Terminal)
item.description: Ships conclude_event, the last lifecycle transition. This is the final folder in the collection's main path — a full pass through Auth -> ... -> T17 exercises every RPC shipped by QA0 through T17 (QA12's tiebreak sub-flow excepted, per that folder's own note).

request.description: T17's conclude_event(p_event_id): organizer-only, terminal active -> concluded transition. Requires events.winner_participant_id to already be set (declare_winner, T16a). Stamps status=concluded and concluded_at.

Re-calling conclude_event on an already-concluded event must be rejected — both by this RPC's own status check and, as a backstop, by T6's events_status_transition_guard trigger (only draft->active->concluded is legal; concluded is terminal). Expects a 400 check_violation.
